pairs: Therefore, interrupting an explanation of the basics of Christ,
ad perfectiora feramur, non rursum jacientes fundamentum pœnitentiæ ab operibus mortuis,
let us consider what is more advanced, not presenting again the fundamentals of repentance from dead works,
and also of the imposition of hands,
and of the resurrection of the dead,
Impossibile est enim eos qui semel sunt illuminati,
For it is impossible for those who were once illuminated,
and have even tasted of the heavenly gift,
et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti,
and have become sharers in the Holy Spirit,
who, despite having tasted the good Word of God and the virtues of the future age,
to be renewed again to penance,
rursus renovari ad pœnitentiam, rursum crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes.
since they are crucifying again in themselves the Son of God and are still maintaining pretenses.
Terra enim sæpe venientem super se bibens imbrem,
For the earth accepts a blessing from God,
by drinking in the rain that often falls upon it,
a quibus colitur, accipit benedictionem a Deo:
and by producing plants that are useful to those by whom it is cultivated.
and is closest to what is accursed;
Confidimus autem de vobis dilectissimi meliora, et viciniora saluti: tametsi ita loquimur.
But from you, most beloved, we are confident that there will be things better and closer to salvation; even though we speak in this way.
such that he would forget your work
and the love that you have shown in his name.
Cupimus autem unumquemque vestrum eamdem ostentare sollicitudinem ad expletionem spei usque in finem:
Yet we desire that each one of you display the same solicitude toward the fulfillment of hope, even unto the end,
so that you may not be slow to act,
but instead may be imitators of those who,
For God, in making promises to Abraham,
per quem juraret, majorem, juravit per semetipsum,
(because he had no one greater by whom he might swear),
and multiplying, I shall multiply you.”
And in this way, by enduring patiently,
Homines enim per majorem sui jurant:
For men swear by what is greater than themselves,
et omnis controversiæ eorum finis, ad confirmationem, est juramentum.
and an oath as confirmation is the end of all their controversy.
In quo abundantius volens Deus ostendere pollicitationis hæredibus, immobilitatem consilii sui, interposuit jusjurandum:
In this matter, God, wanting to reveal more thoroughly the immutability of his counsel to the heirs of the promise, interposed an oath,
so that by two immutable things,
in which it is impossible for God to lie,
we may have the strongest solace:
qui confugimus ad tenendam propositam spem,
we who have fled together so as to hold fast to the hope set before us.
quam sicut anchoram habemus animæ tutam
This we have as an anchor of the soul,
et incedentem usque ad interiora velaminis,
which advances even to the interior of the veil,
ubi præcursor pro nobis introivit Jesus,
to the place where the forerunner Jesus has entered on our behalf,
secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum.
so as to become the High Priest for eternity, according to the order of Melchizedek.
